newsitem.title: DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: Shots fired as strike hits Dominican town.
newsitem.headline: Shots fired as strike hits Dominican town.

text.p: Protesting workers burned tires and fired shots at Dominican police on Tuesday during a 48-hour strike which closed down most of San Francisco de Macoris, police and radio reports said.
Police said at least 20 people were arrested and that shots were fired during street clashes but reported no injuries.

Local radio station Radio Popular said masked demonstrators fired shots at police in the district of Pueblo Nuevo on the northern rim of the town, 117 miles (186 km) northeast of the capital Santo Domingo.
It was not immediately clear if police shot back, although some radio reports spoke of "exchanges of gunfire".
Local journalists told Reuters by telephone that protestors had also burned tires and that home-made bombs had been heard going off, although the town was calm late Tuesday.
They said factories, banks and schools had closed for the strike, called by about 20 popular organisations and set to continue on Wednesday.
Strike leaders were demanding the government build a hospital and airport in the area, extend electricity services to rural areas and take measures to lower the cost of living.

The Dominican government sent in army and police units on Saturday to quell any unrest, saying the strike was politically inspired and blaming the opposition Dominican Revolutionary Party (PRD). The PRD on Tuesday denied any link to the protests.
